newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH BANKING CLIMATE FALLS IN DECEMBER - SURVEY.
newsitem.headline: POLISH BANKING CLIMATE FALLS IN DECEMBER - SURVEY.

text.p: Poland's banking climate index fell 11 points in December to 40.4 points, a poll released on Tuesday by the private Pentor intitute showed.
"We are observing a significant break in the growth trend of the banking climate," Eugeniusz Smilowski told a news conference, adding however the drop was likely to be only temporary.
Smilowski said the lower banking climate was caused in part by weaker credit action and a decrease in the size of bank deposits.
In November the index, based on a scale of minus 100 to plus 100, eased 1.1 point to 51.4 points from October's record high.
The Pentor survey, which polled 211 bank managers, is commissioned monthly by the Polish Banking Association (ZBP).
